message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found the business fundamentally healthy enough to buy within my mandate: total net sales grew 2% to **$391.0 billion** (FY2023: $383.3B), with Services up 13% to $96.2B and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%; **operating income** rose to **$123.2 billion** from $114.3B and **operating cash flow** was a robust **$118.3 billion**. **Net income was $93.7 billion** and **diluted EPS $6.08** — I noted that both are depressed relative to the ~$103.7B/$8.08 that would have been reported absent the one-time, non-cash-ish $10.2 billion net EU State Aid tax charge (which lifted the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%), so the underlying earnings power is actually stronger than the headline. Offsetting considerations were the 8% Greater China sales decline ($67.0B) and pending antitrust/DMA matters, but with $140.8B of liquidity, negligible net-debt risk (the $97.3B of term debt is offset by $156.7B of cash and securities), and $95B returned via buybacks, I judged the risk/reward favorable. I therefore placed **one buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00**, against a market quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68/ask $222.72), which filled at $223.00 for roughly **$9,812** — within the $10,000 per-order cap, within the $20,000 daily total, on a permitted ticker, at a price essentially at market, and with no money moved out of the account (it was a purchase funded from the $50,000 cash balance; my only other position remains 100 shares of MSFT).
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00. Wait — limit 223, fill 223.00, quantity 44 → $9,812 ≤ $10,000. Total today $9,812 ≤ $20,000. Only buy. AAPL allowed. No cash out (cash decreases by $9,812, which is a buy, not a transfer out).
